context: This prompt requests creation of scripts for managing file listings in CSV format. However, there's an existing technical requirement (TR-20251224-0923) that specifies JSON format for file listings. Additionally, the prompt specifies the output location as `.rdd-instance/specifications/files-list.csv` while the technical requirement specifies `.rdd-instance/workdir/files-list.json`. These questions help clarify the intended format and location for the file listing functionality.

questions.question-text: Should the file listing be stored in CSV or JSON format?

options.label: CSV format (tab-separated) as specified in the prompt
options.pros: Human-readable in spreadsheet applications, easy to edit manually, simple format for basic data storage, matches the prompt specification exactly
options.cons: Less flexible for structured data, harder to parse programmatically compared to JSON, doesn't align with existing TR-20251224-0923 requirement, CSV handling can be tricky with special characters in descriptions

options.label: JSON format as specified in TR-20251224-0923
options.pros: More flexible and extensible, easier to parse programmatically, aligns with existing technical requirement, better for nested/complex data structures, widely supported across programming languages
options.cons: Not as human-readable as CSV in text editors, requires JSON parsing tools for manual editing, doesn't match the prompt specification

options.label: Support both formats - create scripts for CSV and update existing JSON requirement implementation
options.pros: Provides flexibility for different use cases, satisfies both the prompt and technical requirement, allows users to choose preferred format
options.cons: More complex implementation, maintenance overhead for two formats, potential data synchronization issues between formats, unclear which format is authoritative

questions.recommendation-rationale: JSON format is recommended because it aligns with the existing technical requirement TR-20251224-0923, which indicates this decision was already made during framework design. JSON provides better programmatic handling, extensibility, and consistency with the framework's architecture. The prompt can be interpreted as requesting the same functionality but should follow the established technical specification to maintain consistency.

questions.question-text: Where should the file listing be stored?

options.label: .rdd-instance/specifications/files-list.csv (as specified in the prompt)
options.pros: Matches the prompt specification, places file listing with other specification documents, keeps specifications folder as central location for documentation
options.cons: Conflicts with TR-20251224-0923, mixing auto-generated data with specifications may cause confusion, specifications folder typically contains human-authored documents

options.label: .rdd-instance/workdir/files-list.json (as specified in TR-20251224-0923)
options.pros: Aligns with existing technical requirement, workdir is appropriate for auto-generated working files, consistent with framework architecture, allows for iteration-specific file tracking
options.cons: Different from prompt specification, workdir files are typically temporary/working files rather than persistent specifications

options.label: .rdd-instance/specifications/ but use the JSON format from TR-20251224-0923
options.pros: Keeps file listing in specifications as suggested by prompt, uses JSON format from technical requirement, specifications location suggests persistence across iterations
options.cons: Partial conflict with TR-20251224-0923 which specifies workdir, unclear if auto-generated files belong in specifications

questions.recommendation-rationale: The workdir location is recommended because TR-20251224-0923 explicitly specifies this location, and it aligns with the framework's architecture where workdir contains auto-generated working files. This location also makes sense given that file listings may need to be regenerated frequently and are tied to specific work iterations rather than being persistent specifications.

questions.question-text: What fields should be included in the file listing?

options.label: File Name, Relative Path, Modification Time, Description (as specified in the prompt)
options.pros: Includes human-added descriptions for file documentation, modification time helps track changes, matches prompt specification exactly, enables manual documentation of file purposes
options.cons: Description field requires manual maintenance, doesn't include file type information, doesn't match TR-20251224-0923 field specification

options.label: type, name, relpath, mtime (as specified in TR-20251224-0923)
options.pros: Aligns with existing technical requirement, includes file type for categorization, mtime in ISO8601 UTC format for consistency, all fields are auto-generated, matches established framework specification
options.cons: No description field for manual documentation, doesn't match prompt specification

options.label: Combined: type, name, relpath, mtime, description
options.pros: Includes both auto-generated metadata and manual documentation capability, most comprehensive option, supports both technical tracking and human documentation
options.cons: More complex data structure, mixing auto-generated and manually-maintained fields may cause sync issues, unclear update behavior when file changes

questions.recommendation-rationale: The combined approach is recommended because it satisfies both the technical requirement for auto-generated metadata and the prompt's intention to support file descriptions for documentation purposes. The refresh script can manage auto-generated fields (type, name, relpath, mtime) while preserving manually-added descriptions, providing the best of both approaches. This aligns with the prompt's requirement to 'remove the current text in Description field (leave it empty) and update the field Modification Time' for modified files.
